findings: The zero-parameter old-turn theorem distinguishes k=j+1 from every other k!=j. At the successor corner the incoming enlarged edge is the return edge, whose value at zero is the original edge P j. In the other case both actual incident edges are unchanged. Thus the changed incoming edge at the successor is not overlooked.

Parent G1 makes every retained old turn nonzero. Continuity of each specified turn at zero, followed by a finite intersection over all old labels, proves simultaneous turn persistence. No genericity assumption is made at the whole zero-parameter inserted tuple.
The actual return direction is edge P j-epsilon*q. Its two-sided limit at zero is proved directly from continuity, with no orientation restriction on q.

The final theorem combines the old-turn neighborhood and the local nonzero parent-turn sign neighborhood by min. On that common positive interval it exports all retained old turns, the two exact new turns, sign det(incoming,return)=turn P j, and the opposite ordered sign=-turn P j.

The only geometric premise of the final result is parent G1, with n>=3 and arbitrary q. Admissibility is not needed for these equalities or old-turn persistence; when q is degenerate the theorem does not claim that the two new turns are nonzero. The source admissible case is included without a new caller premise.
